title: A look at React, Vue and Svelte, from where Angular stands

videos.script:
This course ends by looking at the other three frameworks of this track. It builds one small card four times, and compares what it sees.

{{angular}} First the card in Angular, in a new project, with a signal, two computed values and a template.

{{react}} Then React. The card is a function, and it runs again every time the state changes, twice in development.

{{vue}} Then Vue, with its script and template in one file. Its setup runs once, as Angular's constructor did.

{{svelte}} Then Svelte, a compiler. Most of its work is done while building, and its page carries the least code of the four.

{{again}} So there are two ways to update a page. Three of the frameworks follow who read a value, and React runs the component again and compares.

{{box}} Angular brings its router, forms, HTTP and server rendering in one box. The others choose, and the lesson weighs what that costs in the page.

{{choosing}} Last, how a team chooses, and the long list of what this course taught that is not Angular's at all.
